Limits DoS from unbounded manifest growth. */\n106\t  MAX_K_MANIFEST_BLOCKS: 1000, // 1000 manifest blocks ≈ 195 MB of manifest data\n107\t  /** Maximum UTF-8 encoded filename length in bytes (T2). Chosen to fit within R1's 256-byte payload. */\n108\t  MAX_FILENAME_BYTES: 128,\n109\t  /** Maximum UTF-8 encoded MIME type length in bytes (T2). Chosen to fit within R1's 256-byte payload. */\n110\t  MAX_MIMETYPE_BYTES: 58,\n111\t  /** Maximum UTF-8 codepoint count for filename (T2). A UTF-8 string can use up to 4 bytes per codepoint. */\n112\t  MAX_FILENAME_CODEPOINTS: 32, // 32 × 4 = 128, guarantees never exceeds MAX_FILENAME_BYTES\n113\t  /** Maximum UTF-8 codepoint count for MIME type (T2). */\n114\t  MAX_MIMETYPE_CODEPOINTS: 14, // 14 × 4 = 56, fits within MAX_MIMETYPE_BYTES\n115\t} as const;\n116\t\n117\t/**\n118\t * Calculate K_manifest from blockCount and blockHashLen.\n119\t *\n120\t * K_manifest is the number of blocks needed to store the block hash manifest.\n121\t * The manifest contains blockCount × blockHashLen bytes (all block hashes),\n122\t * divided into blocks of size BLOCK (196608 bytes = K × L).\n123\t *\n124\t * Formula: K_manifest = ceil(blockCount × blockHashLen / BLOCK)\n125\t *\n126\t * @param blockCount - Number of data blocks (from beacon)\n127\t * @param blockHashLen - Length of each block hash in bytes (from beacon)\n128\t * @returns Number of blocks needed to store the manifest\n129\t */\n130\tfunction calculateKManifest(blockCount: number, blockHashLen: number): number {\n131\t  const BLOCK = 196608; // K × L where K=768, L=256 (from core/params.ts)\n132\t  const manifestBytes = blockCount * blockHashLen;\n133\t  return Math.ceil(manifestBytes / BLOCK);\n134\t}\n135\t\n136\t/**\n137\t * Device context for K validation logging.\n138\t */\n139\texport interface DeviceContext {\n140\t  /** Device signature from GE benchmark cache */\n141\t  deviceSignature: string;\n142\t  /** User agent string */\n143\t  userAgent: string;\n144\t  /** Platform identifier */\n145\t  platform: string;\n146\t}\n147\t\n148\t/**\n149\t * Parse a beacon from bytes.\n150\t *\n151\t * Beacon format: [body fields...][crc32(4)]\n152\t * The CRC-32 covers all beacon body fields and MUST be validated before\n153\t * any metadata (including streamId) is trusted.\n154\t *\n155\t * **Validation order is critical:**\n156\t * 1. Read all fields (no validation yet)\n157\t * 2. Validate CRC-32 (if this fails, ALL other values are suspect)\n158\t * 3. Then do bounds/K/quota checks (safe now because CRC validated)\n159\t *\n160\t * @param bytes - Beacon payload bytes (after QR decoding and header stripping)\n161\t * @param localKMax - This device's validation logging\n164\t * @throws {BeaconValidationError} If any field fails validation or CRC-32 mismatch\n165\t */\n166\texport function parseBeacon(\n167\t  bytes: Uint8Array,\n168\t  localKMax: number,\n169\t  availableQuota: number,\n170\t  deviceContext?: DeviceContext\n171\t): BeaconMeta {\n172\t  let offset = 0;\n173\t\n174\t  const readU32 = (): number => {\n175\t    const value = (bytes[offset]! << 24) |\n176\t                 (bytes[offset + 1]! << 16) |\n177\t                 (bytes[offset + 2]! << 8) |\n178\t                 bytes[offset + 3]!;\n179\t    offset += 4;\n180\t    return value >>> 0; // Force unsigned\n181\t  };\n182\t\n183\t  const readU24 = (): number => {\n184\t    const value = (bytes[offset]! << 16) |\n185\t                 (bytes[offset + 1]! << 8) |\n186\t                 bytes[offset + 2]!;\n187\t    offset += 3;\n188\t    return value >>> 0;\n189\t  };\n190\t\n191\t  const readU16 = (): number => {\n192\t    const value = (bytes[offset]! << 8) | bytes[offset + 1]!;\n193\t    offset += 2;\n194\t    return value >>> 0;\n195\t  };\n196\t\n197\t  const readU8 = (): number => {\n198\t    const value = bytes[offset]!;\n199\t    offset += 1;\n200\t    return value;\n201\t  };\n202\t\n203\t  const readBytes = (n: number): Uint8Array => {\n204\t    const value = bytes.subarray(offset, offset + n);\n205\t    offset += n;\n206\t    return value;\n207\t  };\n208\t\n209\t  const readString = (maxLen: number) => {\n210\t    const len = readU8();\n211\t    if (len > maxLen) {\n212\t      throw new BeaconValidationError(\n213\t        'E-META-BOUNDS',\n214\t        `String length ${len} exceeds maximum ${maxLen}`,\n215\t        {length: len, max: maxLen}\n216\t      );\n217\t    }\n218\t    const strBytes = readBytes(len);\n219\t    // Decode as UTF-8\n220\t    const decoder = new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true});\n221\t    try {\n222\t      return decoder.decode(strBytes);\n223\t    } catch (e) {\n224\t      throw new BeaconValidationError(\n225\t        'E-META-BOUNDS',\n226\t        'Invalid UTF-8 in string field',\n227\t        {}\n228\t      );\n229\t    }\n230\t  };\n231\t\n232\t  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ STEP 1: Read all fields (no validation yet)\n233\t\n234\t  const streamId = readU32();\n235\t  const wireVersion = readU8();\n236\t  // originalSize: 6 bytes, 48-bit (original uncompressed file size)\n237\t  const originalSize = ((readU8() << 40) & 0xff0000000000) |\n238\t                       ((readU32() << 8) & 0xffffffffff00) |\n239\t                       (readU8() & 0xff);\n240\t  // payloadLen: 6 bytes, 48-bit (actual payload length after compression)\n241\t  const payloadLen = ((readU8() << 40) & 0xff0000000000) |\n242\t                     ((readU32() << 8) & 0xffffffffff00) |\n243\t                     (readU8() & 0xff);\n244\t\n245\t  const blockSize = readU24();\n246\t  const blockCount = readU24();\n247\t  const fragmentLen = readU16();\n248\t  const degreeCap = readU8();\n249\t  const flags = readU8();\n250\t  const blockHashLen = readU8();\n251\t  const wholeFileHash = readBytes(32); // Fixed 32-byte whole file hash\n252\t  const manifestHash = readBytes(4); // Fixed 4-byte manifest hash (CRC-32)\n253\t\n254\t  // Variable fields\n255\t  const filename = readString(BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILENAME_BYTES);\n256\t  const mimeType = readString(BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_MIMETYPE_BYTES);\n257\t\n258\t  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ STEP 2: CRC-32 validation (MUST pass before any beacon values are trusted)\n259\t\n260\t  const CRC_SIZE = 4;\n261\t  const beaconBodySize = offset;\n262\t  const expectedSize = beaconBodySize + CRC_SIZE;\n263\t\n264\t  if (bytes.length !== expectedSize) {\n265\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n266\t      'E-CRC-LENGTH',\n267\t      `Beacon size ${bytes.length} != expected ${expectedSize} (body+CRC)`,\n268\t      {actual: bytes.length, expected: expectedSize}\n269\t    );\n270\t  }\n271\t\n272\t  // Read the CRC-32 from the last 4 bytes\n273\t  const storedCrc = ((bytes[offset]! << 24) |\n274\t                    (bytes[offset + 1]! << 16) |\n275\t                    (bytes[offset + 2]! << 8) |\n276\t                    bytes[offset + 3]!) >>> 0; // Force unsigned\n277\t\n278\t  // Calculate CRC-32 over the beacon body (everything except the last 4 bytes)\n279\t  const calculatedCrc = crc32(bytes.subarray(0, beaconBodySize));\n280\t\n281\t  if (storedCrc !== calculatedCrc) {\n282\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n283\t      'E-CRC-MISMATCH',\n284\t      `Beacon CRC-32 mismatch: stored=${storedCrc} calculated=${calculatedCrc}`,\n285\t      {stored: storedCrc, calculated: calculatedCrc}\n286\t    );\n287\t  }\n288\t\n289\t  // (originalSize > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILE_SIZE) {\n293\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n294\t      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n295\t      `Declared original size (${originalSize}) exceeds maximum (${BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILE_SIZE})`,\n296\t      {originalSize, max: BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILE_SIZE}\n297\t    );\n298\t  }\n299\t\n300\t  // T1: originalSize must fit in available quota\n301\t  if (originalSize > availableQuota) {\n302\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n303\t      'E-QUOTA-PREFLIGHT',\n304\t      `Original size (${originalSize}) exceeds available quota (${availableQuota})`,\n305\t      {originalSize, availableQuota}\n306\t    );\n307\t  }\n308\t\n309\t  // T1: payloadLen bounds check (same limit as originalSize)\n310\t  if (payloadLen > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILE_SIZE) {\n311\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n312\t      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n313\t      `Declared payload length (${payloadLen}) exceeds maximum (${BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILE_SIZE})`,\n314\t      {payloadLen, max: BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILE_SIZE}\n315\t    );\n316\t  }\n317\t\n318\t  // T1: payloadLen must fit in available quota\n319\t  if (payloadLen > availableQuota) {\n320\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n321\t      'E-QUOTA-PREFLIGHT',\n322\t      `Payload length (${payloadLen}) exceeds available quota (${availableQuota})`,\n323\t      {payloadLen, availableQuota}\n324\t    );\n325\t  }\n326\t\n327\t  // Sanity: payloadLen should be ≤ originalSize (compression can only reduce)\n328\t  if (payloadLen > originalSize) {\n329\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n330\t      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n331\t      `Payload length (${payloadLen}) cannot exceed original size (${originalSize})`,\n332\t      {payloadLen, originalSize}\n333\t    );\n334\t  }\n335\t\n336\t  // T1: blockCount bounds check\n337\t  if (blockCount > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_BLOCK_COUNT) {\n338\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n339\t      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n340\t      `Block count (${blockCount}) exceeds maximum (${BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_BLOCK_COUNT})`,\n341\t      {blockCount, max: BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_BLOCK_COUNT}\n342\t    );\n343\t  }\n344\t\n345\t  // T1: K_manifest bounds check (bf-5fs)\n346\t  // blockCount_manifest is the number of blocks needed to store the block hash manifest.\n347\t  // Unbounded blockCount_manifest is a DoS vector: with MAX_BLOCK_COUNT (16.7M) and blockHashLen=4,\n348\t  // the manifest would require 340 blocks (~66 MB manifest data, ~24 KB matrix per block).\n349\t  const blockCountManifest = calculateKManifest(blockCount, blockHashLen);\n350\t  if (blockCountManifest > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_K_MANIFEST_BLOCKS) {\n351\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n352\t      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n353\t      `Manifest block count (${blockCountManifest}) exceeds maximum (${BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_K_MANIFEST_BLOCKS}). ` +\n354\t      `This would require ${blockCountManifest} blocks (${(blockCountManifest * 196608 / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(1)} MB) ` +\n355\t      `to store the manifest for ${blockCount} data blocks.`,\n356\t      {\n357\t        blockCount,\n358\t        blockHashLen,\n359\t        blockCountManifest,\n360\t        max: BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_K_MANIFEST_BLOCKS\n361\t      }\n362\t    );\n363\t  }\n364\t\n365\t  // Sanity: blockSize should be reasonable\n366\t  if (blockSize < 1 || blockSize > 10_485_760) { // Max 10 MB per block\n367\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n368\t      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n369\t      `Invalid block size: ${blockSize}`,\n370\t      {blockSize}\n371\t    );\n372\t  }\n373\t\n374\t  // T1: Wire version compatibility check\n375\t  if (wireVersion !== WIRE_VERSION) {\n376\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n377\t      'E-VERSION',\n378\t      `Wire version mismatch: sender is ${wireVersion}, receiver is ${WIRE_VERSION}`,\n379\t      {senderVersion: wireVersion, receiverVersion: WIRE_VERSION}\n380\t    );\n381\t  }\n382\t\n383\t  // T1: L must match wire constant for this version\n384\t  if (fragmentLen !== L) {\n385\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n386\t      'E-VERSION',\n387\t      `Fragment length L mismatch: sender declared ${fragmentLen}, wire constant is ${L}`,\n388\t      {senderL: fragmentLen, wireConstantL: L, wireVersion}\n389\t    );\n390\t  }\n391\t\n392\t  // T1: Secondary sanity check (should never fire if above checks pass)\n393\t  if (fragmentLen < 1 || fragmentLen > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_L) {\n394\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n395\t      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n396\t      `Fragment length L (${fragmentLen}) outside valid range [1, ${BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_L}]`,\n397\t      {L: fragmentLen, max: BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_L}\n398\t    );\n399\t  }\n400\t\n401\t  // Sanity: degreeCap should be within reasonable bounds (D25 says 64)\n402\t  if (degreeCap < 1 || degreeCap > 256) {\n403\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n404\t      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n405\t      `Invalid degree cap: ${degreeCap}`,\n406\t      {degreeCap}\n407\t    );\n408\t  }\n409\t\n410\t  // Sanity: blockHashLen should be reasonable (SHA-256 truncated to 4 bytes per plan)\n411\t  if (blockHashLen < 1 || blockHashLen > 64) {\n412\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n413\t      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n414\t      `Invalid block hash length: ${blockHashLen}`,\n415\t      {blockHashLen}\n416\t    );\n417\t  }\n418\t\n419\t  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ STEP 4: D26/T1: K validation\n420\t\n421\t  // Derive K from blockSize and L\n422\t  const kValidation = validateBeaconK(blockSize, fragmentLen, localKMax, deviceContext);\n423\t\n424\t  if (!kValidation.acceptable) {\n425\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n426\t      kValidation.error!.code,\n427\t      kValidation.error!.message,\n428\t      kValidation.error!.details\n429\t    );\n430\t  }\n431\t\n432\t  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ STEP 5: Sanity checks\n433\t\n434\t  // Sanity: blockCount × blockSize should approximately equal payloadLen\n435\t  // (last block may be short, so allow ±1 block tolerance)\n436\t  const estimatedSize = (blockCount - 1) * blockSize;\n437\t  if (payloadLen < estimatedSize - blockSize || payloadLen > blockCount * blockSize + blockSize) {\n438\t    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n439\t      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n440\t      `Inconsistent beacon: payloadLen=${payloadLen}, blockCount=${blockCount}, blockSize=${blockSize}`,\n441\t      {payloadLen, blockCount, blockSize}\n442\t    );\n443\t  }\n444\t\n445\t  return {\n446\t    streamId,\n447\t    wireVersion,\n448\t    originalSize,\n449\t    payloadLen,\n450\t    blockSize,\n451\t    blockCount,\n452\t    fragmentLen,\n453\t    degreeCap,\n454\t    flags,\n455\t    blockHashLen,\n456\t    wholeFileHash,\n457\t    manifestHash,\n458\t    filename,\n459\t    mimeType,\n460\t  };\n461\t}\n462\t\n463\t/**\n464\t * Sanitize a filename for export (T2).\n465\t *\n466\t * **Truncation rules (T2):**\n467\t * 1. Strip path separators, control bytes, and leading dots (security)\n468\t * 2. Truncate to MAX_FILENAME_CODEPOINTS (32 UTF-8 codepoints max)\n469\t * 3. If truncated, preserve filename extension when possible\n470\t * 4. Validate final UTF-8 encoding fits in MAX_FILENAME_BYTES (128 bytes)\n471\t * 5. MAX_FILENAME_BYTES ensures the beacon fits in R1's 256-byte payload\n477\t *\n478\t * @param filename - Attacker-supplied filename from beacon\n479\t * @returns Sanitized filename safe for filesystem export and beacon encoding\n480\t */\n481\texport function sanitizeFilename(filename: string): string {\n482\t  // Step 1: Remove path separators (prevents directory traversal)\n483\t  let sanitized = filename.replace(/[\\/\\\\]/g, '_');\n484\t\n485\t  // Step 2: Remove control bytes (0x00-0x1F, 0x7F) — invalid on most filesystems\n486\t  sanitized = sanitized.replace(/[\\x00-\\x1F\\x7F]/g, '');\n487\t\n488\t  // Step 3: Strip leading dots (avoid hidden files on Unix, prevent dotfiles attack)\n489\t  sanitized = sanitized.replace(/^\\.+/g, '');\n490\t\n491\t  // Step 4: Truncate to MAX_FILENAME_CODEPOINTS (32 codepoints)\n492\t  if (sanitized.length > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILENAME_CODEPOINTS) {\n493\t    // Try to preserve extension: find last dot and keep extension\n494\t    const lastDot = sanitized.lastIndexOf('.');\n495\t\n496\t    if (lastDot > 0 && lastDot < BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILENAME_CODEPOINTS - 5) {\n497\t      // Keep extension: truncate base, preserve \".ext\"\n498\t      const ext = sanitized.substring(lastDot);\n499\t      const baseAllowed = BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILENAME_CODEPOINTS - ext.length;\n500\t      sanitized = sanitized.substring(0, baseAllowed) + ext;\n501\t    } else {\n502\t      // No extension or extension too long: simple truncate\n503\t      sanitized = sanitized.substring(0, BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILENAME_CODEPOINTS);\n504\t    }\n505\t  }\n506\t\n507\t  // Step 5: Validate UTF-8 byte length fits in MAX_FILENAME_BYTES\n508\t  const utf8Bytes = new TextEncoder().encode(sanitized);\n509\t  if (utf8Bytes.length > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILENAME_BYTES) {\n510\t    // Byte overflow: truncate conservatively to UTF-8 safe boundary\n511\t    // Conservative: each codepoint can be up to 4 bytes, so truncate to codepoints that fit\n512\t    let byteLen = 0;\n513\t    let cpIndex = 0;\n514\t    for (let i = 0; i < sanitized.length; i++) {\n515\t      const cpBytes = new TextEncoder().encode(sanitized[i]).length;\n516\t      if (byteLen + cpBytes > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILENAME_BYTES) break;\n517\t      byteLen += cpBytes;\n518\t      cpIndex = i + 1;\n519\t    }\n520\t    sanitized = sanitized.substring(0, cpIndex);\n521\t  }\n522\t\n523\t  // Step 6: Fallback if empty after sanitization\n524\t  if (!sanitized) {\n525\t    sanitized = 'received-file';\n526\t  }\n527\t\n528\t  return sanitized;\n529\t}\n530\t\n531\t/**\n532\t * Check if resume should be disabled based on beacon flags.\n533\t *\n534\t * When compression is enabled, the sender MUST set BeaconFlags.ResumeDisabled\n535\t * because non-deterministic compression makes block boundaries unstable across\n536\t * sender restarts. This prevents silent corruption of the receiver's bitmap.\n537\t *\n538\t * **How this works:**\n539\t * 1. Sender enables compression → sets both Compressed and ResumeDisabled flags\n540\t * 2. Receiver receives beacon → checks isResumeDisabled() → returns true\n541\t * 3. Receiver suppresses resume UI and does NOT persist bitmap/metadata\n542\t * 4. If interrupted, user must restart transfer from beginning (safe, no corruption)\n543\t *\n544\t * **Why this is necessary:**\n545\t * CompressionStream offers no determinism guarantee. After a sender restart and\n546\t * E11 staging reaping, re-compression may produce different bytes → different\n547\t * block boundaries → different hashes → the receiver's persisted bitmap would\n548\t * become silently invalid.\n549\t *\n550\t * Solution implemented: Option B from bf-3k90 evaluation\n551\t * - Privacy (T4) preserved: no staging persistence\n552\t * - Correctness preserved: explicitly disabling unsafe resume\n553\t * - Low complexity: ~50-100 lines vs. 300-1200 for alternatives\n554\t *\n555\t * Reference: docs/notes/bf-3k90-compression-resume-solution-evaluation.md (Option B)\n556\t *            docs/notes/bf-2vke-compression-resume-t4-reap-interaction.md\n557\t *            docs/notes/bf-17s0-resume-compression-conflict.md\n558\t *\n559\t * @param flags - Beacon flags byte from received beacon\n560\t * @returns true if resume is disabled (compression enabled), false otherwise\n561\t */\n562\texport function isResumeDisabled(flags: number): boolean {\n563\t  return (flags & BeaconFlags.ResumeDisabled) !== 0;\n564\t}\n565\t\n566\t/**\n567\t * Encode a beacon from metadata.\n568\t *\n569\t * Serializes beacon metadata into bytes and appends a CRC-32 checksum\n570\t * over the beacon body for integrity validation.\n571\t *\n572\t * **SENDER CONSTRAINT:** When constructing a BeaconMeta object to pass to this function:\n573\t * - If compression is enabled, you MUST set both flags:\n574\t *   `flags = BeaconFlags.Compressed | BeaconFlags.ResumeDisabled`\n575\t * - This is required because CompressionStream offers no determinism guarantee\n576\t *   across browser restarts, making resume unsafe (see below)\n577\t *\n578\t * **Why compression disables resume:**\n579\t * Non-deterministic compression means that after a sender restart and E11 staging\n580\t * reaping, re-compression may produce different bytes → different block boundaries\n581\t * → different hashes → the receiver's persisted bitmap becomes silently invalid.\n582\t *\n583\t * Solution: The sender signals \"no resume available\" via the beacon flag, and new BeaconValidationError(\n596\t      'E-VERSION',\n597\t      `Cannot encode beacon for wire version ${meta.wireVersion}, this implementation is ${WIRE_VERSION}`,\n598\t      {requestedVersion: Everything else is explanation.\n31\t\n32\t---\n33\t\n34\t## 1. Objective\n35\t\n36\t> **A static website that accepts a file from the user and turns it into a visual\n37\t> transmission on screen, which a second device running the same page receives through\n38\t> its camera and reconstructs into the original file.**\n39\t>\n40\t> **It must handle large files — on the order of multiple gigabytes.**\n41\t\n42\t- **Static.** No backend. Files on a CDN, works offline, auditable once and trusted\n43\t  thereafter. There is nowhere to upload anything *to*.\n44\t- **Same page, both roles.** One deployment; the user picks sender or receiver.\n45\t- **Screen → camera is the only channel.** Strictly one-way, lossy, low-bandwidth.\n46\t- **Multi-gigabyte.** The requirement that most shapes the architecture (§3).\n47\t\n48\t### 1.1 The honest framing of \"multiple gigabytes\"\n49\t\n50\tMulti-GB support is an **architectural** requirement, not a performance promise. The\n51\tdesign must never *forbid* a large file, run out of memory, or blow up super-linearly.\n52\tBut the channel's physics are what they are:\n53\t\n54\t| File size | Stage 1 (30 KB/s) | Stage 2 (60 KB/s) | Stage 3 (106 KB/s) |\n55\t|---|---|---|---|\n56\t| 100 MB | 57 min | 28 min | 16 min |\n57\t| **1 GB** | **9.7 h** | **4.9 h** | **2.7 h** |\n58\t| **10 GB** | **4.0 days** | **2.0 days** | **27.5 h** |\n59\t| 100 GB | 40.5 days | 20.2 days | 11.4 days |\n60\t| 1 TB | 414 days | 207 days | 117 days |\n61\t\n62\t> All figures are **user-visible file bytes**, not wire bytes. See §13.2 — with\n63\t> compression on, the two differ by 3–10× on compressible input, and quoting the wrong\n64\t> one would overstate throughput.\n65\t\n66\t**Gigabytes are hours-to-days. Terabytes are months.** Three design consequences follow,\n67\tand they are as load-bearing as any coding decision:\n68\t\n69\t1. **Resume is not optional** (D22). Nobody holds a phone for 27 hours.\n70\t2. **Neither side may hold the file in memory** (D20).\n71\t3. **The app states the estimated time before the user commits** (D23). Letting someone\n72\t   start a 40-day transfer without saying so is a product failure, not an edge case.\n73\t\n74\t---\n75\t\n76\t## 2. Glossary\n77\t\n78\tSeveral of these words are overloaded in the surrounding literature, and two of them\n79\t(*block*, *frame*) mean different things in different research documents. Within this\n80\tplan they mean exactly this:\n81\t\n82\t| Term | Meaning here |\n83\t|---|---|\n84\t| **Fragment** | The atomic unit the fountain code operates over. Fixed length **L** for the whole session (D15). |\n85\t| **K** | Number of fragments in one block. Derived as `blockSize / L`; never transmitted (D7). |\n86\t| **Block** | A contiguous slice of the (possibly compressed) payload, cut into K fragments and fountain-coded independently. **Always means this** — never \"fountain block\" or \"QR block\". |\n87\t| **Packet** | One fountain-coded symbol: 13-byte header + L payload bytes. The unit a tile carries. |\n88\t| **Tile** | One QR symbol on screen. Carries exactly one packet. |\n89\t| **Frame** | One displayed image, containing a grid of tiles. **Never** a video frame — those are *camera frames*. |\n90\t| **Camera frame** | One image captured by the receiver's camera. |\n91\t| **Beacon** | A special **packet** carrying file-level metadata instead of payload. Beacon packets are encoded into tiles and mixed into display frames by the frame mixer (D17, §7.2). |\n92\t| **Profile** | A modulation configuration: QR version, module pixel size, tile count. Several coexist per frame (D16). |\n93\t| **Dwell** | How many packets the sender emits for one block before advancing (§8.1). |\n94\t| **Screen px** | A pixel on the *sender's display*. What the renderer controls. |\n95\t| **Camera px** | A pixel in the *receiver's captured frame*. What the decoder actually sees. |\n96\t| **px/module** | **Always CAMERA px per module unless explicitly written \"screen px/module\".** The 4 px/module decode cliff is a *camera*-pixel figure. Conflating the two put every S2/S3 optical run below the cliff — see `../notes/spike-results.md` §S3. |\n97\t| **Magnification** | `camera_px_per_module = screen_px_per_module × M`, where `M` = (capture width across the code region) / (code region width in screen px). A 1920-px-wide landscape code region filling a 1080-px-wide portrait capture gives **M = 0.5625**, so 4 screen px/module is only **2.25 camera px/module**. |\n98\t| **Erasure** | A packet that did not arrive or failed validation. Never a corrupted packet — those are discarded, not used. |\n99\t| **Stage** | A modulation generation: 1 = tiled mono QR, 2 = + RGB tripling, 3 = custom grid codec. |\n100\t| **Pass** | One complete traversal of every block by the sender. |\n101\t\n102\t---\n103\t\n104\t## 3. What multi-gigabyte breaks, and the fix\n105\t\n106\tFour assumptions in the pre-multi-GB design do not survive contact with a 4 GB file.\n107\t\n108\t### 3.1 The fountain decoder does not scale — in TIME, not memory\n109\t\n110\tThis is the correction the plan review surfaced, and it matters because the first\n111\tversion of this section got it half right.\n112\t\n113\tD5 chose an LT code with a **Gaussian elimination** decoder, verified at\n114\t[`sim/`](../research/sim/). GE costs O(K²) in *memory* and O(K³) in *bit operations*.\n115\tThe original block-layer decision sized K from the memory term alone and concluded 4 MB\n116\tblocks (K = 16,384) were fine because the coefficient matrix is only 32 MB.\n117\t\n118\t**The memory term was never the binding constraint. Time is.**\n119\t\n120\tEach arriving packet is reduced against up to `rank` stored pivot rows; each row\n121\toperation XORs the coefficient mask (K/8 bytes) *and* the payload (L bytes). Reaching\n122\tfull rank costs `W = 2 · (K²/2) · (K/8 + L) = K² · (K/8 + L)` bytes of memory traffic,\n123\tand the block only lasts `K·L / R` seconds at wire rate R — so the decoder must\n124\t**sustain**:\n125\t\n126\t```\n127\trequired = W / (K·L/R) = K · (K/8 + L) · R / L    bytes/sec\n128\t```\n129\t\n130\t> The leading factor is **1, not 2** — the 2 and the /2 in `W` cancel. A previous\n131\t> revision of this section printed `2 · K · (K/8 + L) · R / L` and was 2× too\n132\t> pessimistic in every derived figure. Gate **G7** now diffs this section against the\n133\t> model so the class of error cannot recur.\n134\t\n135\tAll figures below are emitted by\n136\t[`sim/ge_cost_model.py`](../research/sim/ge_cost_model.py) — this section quotes the\n137\tmodel rather than reasoning beside it. **All rows at Stage 1 (R = 30 KB/s)**, so they\n138\tare comparable:\n139\t\n140\t| K | L | Block | Matrix | Work/block | Sustained need | |\n141\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n142\t| 1,000 | 1260 | 1.2 MB | 122.1 KB | 1.3 GB | 33.8 MB/s | research baseline |\n143\t| 1,500 | 1260 | 1.8 MB | 274.7 KB | 3.0 GB | 52.9 MB/s | research partitioning ceiling |\n144\t| 4,000 | 1260 | 4.8 MB | 1.9 MB | 26.2 GB | 171.6 MB/s | research called this **\"too slow\"** |\n145\t| **16,384** | **256** | **4.0 MB** | **32.0 MB** | **576.0 GB** | **4.5 GB/s** | **23× over budget** |\n146\t\n147\tThe plan's own evidence base\n148\t([`fountain-codes-and-protocol.md`](../research/fountain-codes-and-protocol.md) §2.6)\n149\tstates: *\"Cost scales as K², so it must be bounded. At K = 4000 the decode work is ~16×\n150\tthat of K = 1000 (~6 GB of XOR) — too slow\"* and recommends *\"source-block partitioning\n151\tabove K ≈ 1500\"*. **K = 16,384 was 11× past that ceiling.**\n152\t\n153\tIt was worse than a simple overshoot: shrinking L to 256 B to fit small tiles made the\n154\tmask term (K/8 = 2048 B) dominate the payload term (256 B) by 8×, so the decode problem\n155\tgot *harder* as a side effect of a decision made for a different reason.\n156\t\n157\t**Two further findings from the model:**\n158\t\n159\t- **A faster wire rate makes decode harder** — same work, less time to do it. So K MUST\n160\t  be sized for the *fastest* stage we intend to reach (Stage 3, 106 KB/s), not the\n161\t  slowest. This is counterintuitive and is why the original error was easy to make.\n162\t- **The sender's cost was unbudgeted too.** §6.3.1 counted QR encode and render but not\n163\t  the fountain XOR. At uncapped harmonic degree and K = 16,384 that is 398 KB of XOR\n164\t  per packet — **91.8 MB/s** at the old 225 packets/s (1 packet/tile), or **183.6 MB/s**\n165\t  at the adopted 450 packets/s (2 packets/tile at R2 nominal), on top of everything\n166\t  else. Hence D25.\n167\t\n168\t**Fix — D19:** K = **768**, L = **256 B**, block = **192.0 KB**.\n169\t\n170\t| | Was | Now |\n171\t|---|---|---|\n172\t| K | 16,384 | **768** |\n173\t| L | 256 B | **256 B** (unchanged — see §3.1.1) |\n174\t| Block | 4 MB | **192.0 KB** |\n175\t| GE matrix | 32.0 MB | **72.0 KB** |\n176\t| Block-layer working set | ~36 MB (claimed) | **264.0 KB** |\n177\t| Sustained need @ Stage 3 | 14.9 GB/s | **114.6 MB/s** |\n178\t\n179\t*Both \"sustained need\" figures are at Stage 3, so they compare like with like. The\n180\t4.5 GB/s in the table above is the same design at Stage 1.*\n181\t\n182\t**K_max at Stage 3 is 1152.** We adopt **768** deliberately below the ceiling —\n183\tD26 requires the sender to assume the weaker receiver, and the 200 MB/s budget has\n184\tbeen measured (S1: 3,260 MB/s desktop). Margin at Stage 3: **1.74×**.\n185\t\n186\t| K | Block | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Stage 3 | |\n187\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n188\t| 512 | 128.0 KB | 19.7 MB/s | 39.3 MB/s | 69.5 MB/s | 2.88× margin |\n189\t| **768** | **192.0 KB** | **32.4 MB/s** | **64.9 MB/s** | **114.6 MB/s** | **adopted, 1.74× margin** |\n190\t| 1024 | 256.0 KB | 47.2 MB/s | 94.4 MB/s | 166.7 MB/s | 1.20× margin |\n191\t| 1152 | 288.0 KB | 55.3 MB/s | 110.6 MB/s | 195.4 MB/s | 1.02× — the ceiling |\n192\t| 1536 | 384.0 KB | 82.6 MB/s | 165.2 MB/s | 291.8 MB/s | 1.5× **over** at Stage 3 |\n193\t\n194\t### 3.1.1 L is set by the *conservative* ladder rung, not the nominal one\n195\t\n196\tA revision of this plan briefly set L = 507 B (\"one packet per v15 tile\") and broke\n197\tD16's ladder. D15's source note states the governing rule plainly: **pick L to fit the\n198\tsmallest tile any profile would use.** At L = 507 the packet is 520 B and the\n199\tconservative rung, v10-L, holds **271 B** — so it could carry **zero** packets, only\n200\tbeacons. That destroys the ladder's one load-bearing property: *a mis-guessed profile\n201\tyields zero; a ladder always yields something.*\n202\t\n203\t**Rungs are therefore defined by packet count, with the QR version chosen to fit** —\n204\tnot the reverse. At L = 256 B, packet = 13 + 256 = **269 B**:\n205\t\n206\t| Rung | Packets | Needs | QR version | Capacity | Waste |\n207\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n208\t| R1 conservative | 1 | 269 B | v10-L | 271 B | 2 B |\n209\t| R2 nominal | 2 | 538 B | v16-L | 586 B | 48 B |\n210\t| R3 aggressive | 3 | 807 B | v20-L | 858 B | 51 B |\n211\t| R4 (probe only) | 4 | 1076 B | v23-L | 1091 B | 15 B |\n212\t\n213\tWaste stays ≤ 51 B on every rung. The pressure that motivated raising L has also\n214\tgone: at K = 768 the mask term is K/8 = 96 B against a 256 B payload (27%), not the\n215\t8× dominance that made L = 256 pathological at K = 16,384.\n216\t\n217\t**A rung MUST carry a whole number of packets.** Partial packets across tiles would\n218\tcouple tiles together and destroy the independence D1 depends on.\n219\t\n220\t### 3.2 Neither side can hold the file in memory\n221\t\n222\tA multi-GB `Uint8Array` is not allocatable (Chrome's `ArrayBuffer` ceiling is ~2 GB;\n223\tSafari's is lower), and would get a phone tab killed regardless.\n224\t\n225\t**Fix — D20:** stream both ends. `File.slice()` on the sender, OPFS on the receiver, one\n226\tblock resident at a time.\n227\t\n228\t### 3.3 The whole-file hash cannot be computed in one pass\n229\t\n230\t`crypto.subtle.digest` has **no streaming API** — it takes one buffer.\n231\t\n232\t**Fix:** per-block hashes (cheap, and they let each block be written as it completes,\n233\tthen verified retroactively once the manifest arrives) plus a mandatory whole-file hash\n234\tfrom an incremental WASM hasher. concept.md constraint 4 makes byte-exact reconstruction\n235\tnon-negotiable and names the whole-file hash as the verification (see §7.2). See §7.4\n236\tfor how this interacts with `streamId`.\n237\t\n238\t### 3.4 Miss recovery gets expensive as blocks multiply\n239\t\n240\tAt 192 KB per block a 4 GB file is ~21,845 blocks. Sequential dwell means a block missed\n241\ton pass 1 waits for pass 2 — hours. **Fix:** the repair code (§8.2), which makes recovery\n242\tsub-minute and is why smaller blocks are affordable.\n243\t\n244\t---\n245\t\n246\t## 4. Decisions\n247\t\n248\t| # | Decision | Rationale | Source |\n249\t|---|---|---|---|\n250\t| **D19** | **Block layer: independent 192.0 KB blocks, K = 768, L = 256 B** | GE cost is bound by *time*, not memory (§3.1). K = 768 keeps pace at Stage 3's 106 KB/s (114.6 MB/s needed, **1.74x margin**) within a conservative 200 MB/s phone-JS budget; matrix is 72.0 KB and the block-layer working set 264.0 KB, flat regardless of file size. K_max is 1152; 768 is deliberate conservatism per D26. **L is set by the conservative ladder rung** (S3.1.1), not the nominal one. What RFC 6330 calls source blocks. | §3.1, `sim/ge_cost_model.py` |\n251\t| **D27** | **The receiver duty-cycles BLOCKS under receiver-side thermal pressure; multi-GB is framed as multi-session** | Measured: a Pixel 6 hit 70 °C and its throttling threshold in **20–30 minutes**, against a §1.1 objective of 27 h–4 days of *continuous* decoding. Duty-cycling must be **block-granular**, not frame-granular: the receiver knows blockIndex from the header (§7.1), so it decodes block N at full attention and skips N+1 entirely. This doubles the number of passes but completes transfers where frame-granular duty cycling would never finish (frame-granular 50% duty on 25% erasure delivers only 0.60 K against the 1.03 K needed at dwell 1.6). No web API exposes SoC temperature, so sustained fps decline is the proxy (E17b). **Throttling discrimination:** Before applying duty-cycling, the receiver MUST distinguish sender-side throttling (E17a) from receiver-side throttling (E17b) using the multi-metric approach specified in `docs/notes/bf-3mnt-thermal-throttling-discrimination.md`. Sender-side throttling is detected when camera fps drops >30% while decode latency stays within +30%; in this case, the receiver MUST NOT duty-cycle. Receiver-side throttling is detected when decode latency increases >50% while camera fps stays within -20%; in this case, D27's block-granular duty-cycling applies. | `spike-results`, R11, `bf-3mnt` |\n252\t| **D25** | **Cap fountain degree at d ≤ 64** | Cuts encoder XOR **7.9×** at the adopted K = 768 (mean degree 106.3 → 13.5): 12.2 MB/s → 1.6 MB/s at 450 packets/s (R2 nominal: 2 packets/tile, 15 tiles, 15 fps). D6 forbids changing the distribution on faith, so it was **simulated**: at the adopted **K = 768** the cap costs **+1.6 points** (1.34% → 2.97% mean, p99 4.2%), and +1.9 pts at K = 1024. There is a cliff below it — cap 32 costs +4.9 pts with a bad p99, cap 16 costs **+55 pts**. 64 is the right side of the cliff with margin. | `sim/degree_cap_sim.py` |\n253\t| **D26** | **K is chosen by the SENDER at session start and MUST be conservative** | Decode cost lands on the receiver, whose CPU the sender cannot know (no back-channel). So the sender MUST assume the weaker device. K = 768 is the default floor; a sender-side setting MAY raise it when the user knows the receiver is a desktop, **but MUST NOT exceed K_MAX = 2048 to maintain I6a's 1 MB block-layer working set constraint**. Working set = K²/8 + K×L (matrix + block); at K = 2048 with L = 256 B this equals exactly 1 MB. The receiver derives K from the beacon and MUST refuse a stream whose K exceeds what it benchmarked locally. | §3.1, `src/core/params.ts` validateK() |\n254\t| **D20** | **Stream both ends; never materialise the file** | Multi-GB `ArrayBuffer` is not allocatable. `File.slice()` sender-side, OPFS receiver-side. | §3.2 |\n255\t| **D21** | **Per-packet header stays 13 bytes: file metadata lives in the beacon** | A 3-byte block index would have cost 23% more header. Moving `payloadLen`, filename, MIME, hash and block count into the periodic beacon pays for it exactly. Payload packets carry only what is needed to *place bytes*. | §7.1 |\n256\t| **D22** | **Resume is mandatory and first-class** | At 2.7–27 h for 1–10 GB, no transfer survives on user patience. Receiver persists the completed-block bitmap; incomplete blocks restart rather than persisting partial GE state. | §1.1, §8.3 |\n257\t| **D23** | **Estimate time before the user commits; refuse or warn at defined thresholds** | Thresholds are numeric (§13.1), not \"a threshold\". Estimate from *measured* rate once acquired. | §1.1 |\n258\t| **D24** | **Frames generated on demand and discarded; nothing pre-rendered** | The LT stream is endless — no finite frame set exists. One pass over 4 GB is ~550,000 frames = **4.2 TB** as `ImageData`. On-demand encode costs ~7% of one core. PRNG-derived indices make the sender **stateless**: frame *N* generates without replaying 1…*N*−1, which is what makes resume and repair nearly free. | §6.3.1 |\n259\t| D1 | **Tiled QR, not single QR** | 15 × v15 QR decode from one 1080p frame in 7.8 ms for ~7.5 KB user-visible payload (at 2 packets/tile: 15 tiles × 2 packets × 256 B = 7,680 B; 8.0 KB includes 13-byte headers). This vs 2,953 B for one v40 — ~2.5× for zero new decoder risk. | `beyond-qr` §10 |\n260\t| D2 | **QR v15 @ ECC L, ~15 tiles** | Bounded by the 4 **camera** px/module cliff (§2 — *not* screen px), not symbology density. EC L because the channel is erasure-dominated — redundancy belongs in the fountain code. L→H would cost 57% of payload for nothing. | `qr-encoding` |\n261\t| D3 | **zxing-wasm decoder, read `.bytes`** | Only credible multi-symbol decoder that returns real bytes — verified against 7 libraries with every byte value: exact in 100% of payloads. Bounded 9–26 ms where jsQR hit 1453 ms. Apache-2.0. | `browser-qr-scanning` |\n262\t| D4 | **node-qrcode encoder, mask pinned** | Pinning the mask is a 4.6–8× encode speedup — a bigger lever than library choice. Worker-safe. | `qr-encoding` |\n263\t| D5 | **LT fountain + harmonic distribution + GF(2) Gaussian elimination** | GE needs +1.2% overhead at K=1000 where peeling needs +180%. ~300 lines. **Re-measured at the adopted K = 768**: +1.34% mean / +2.5% p99 uncapped, +2.97% / +4.2% with D25's cap — inside §13.1's budget. See §18 R1 for the RaptorQ trigger. | `fountain-codes`, `sim/` |\n264\t| D6 | **Harmonic and GE are a coupled pair — never change one alone** | Harmonic + peeling is the worst cell measured and degrades as K grows. Fails only on large inputs, pointing away from the cause. Any change to the distribution (including D25's cap) MUST be simulated first. | `sim/` |\n265\t| D7 | **Index sets derived from a PRNG, never transmitted** | Seeded on `(streamId, blockIndex, seq)`. Zero index bytes on the wire. | `fountain-codes` |\n266\t| D8 | **Compress before blocking, to a staging file** | `CompressionStream` is native and streaming. Compress to OPFS first, then cut into fixed blocks — keeps K constant and derivable. Skip on already-compressed input (sample-detect). Staging MUST be wiped (§12, T4a). **Trade-off: with compression enabled, resume is NOT supported** (§8.3, `notes/bf-17s0-resume-compression-conflict.md`) — `CompressionStream` offers no determinism guarantee, so re-compression after staging is reaped (E11) would produce different blocks and silently corrupt the receiver's state. | `fountain-codes` |\n267\t| D9 | **Display at ≤ half the *measured* camera fps** | PixNet's rule. Faster produces only torn frames. | `beyond-qr` |\n268\t| D10 | **Every frame DC-balanced** | Stops auto-exposure hunting; throughput swings 2.4× on exposure. Also part of the photosensitivity mitigation (§20.1). | `custom-codec` |\n269\t| D11 | **A runtime calibration probe decides luma-vs-colour, not this document** | Two research threads reached opposite conclusions (§6.6). The probe measures the device. | `beyond-qr` §6.6 |\n270\t| D12 | **Dark-on-light, not dual-polarity** | Dual-polarity costs ~50% throughput. OLED ABL means mostly-white loses ~4× brightness — \"light\" means *moderate*. | `pwa-platform` |\n271\t| D13 | **Add to Home Screen is mandatory on iOS** | Safari deletes service-worker caches after 7 days; Home Screen apps are exempt. | `pwa-platform` |\n272\t| D14 | **`exposureCompensation: min`; measure delivered fps, never trust `getSettings()`** | A precondition for D9. Android delivers 15 fps while reporting 30/60; the fix measured 15.0 → 41.6 fps. Absent on iOS — hence \"measured\". | `browser-qr-scanning` §1.4 |\n273\t| D15 | **Fragment length `L` is fixed for the session — not per profile, not ever** | Change L and K changes, invalidating every packet already collected. | `link-adaptation-design` |\n274\t| D16 | **Sender mixes 2–4 robustness profiles *within every frame*; no negotiation in v1** | Packets are fungible, so the sender never has to choose. **Probing is free** — a probe tile that succeeds delivers real payload. Mixed within a frame so profiles cannot alias against camera fps. | `link-adaptation` |\n275\t| D17 | **Conservative beacon profile, re-emitted periodically** | WiFi's lowest basic rate. Enables late join and re-acquisition. Carries all file metadata (D21). | `link-adaptation-design` |\n276\t| D18a | **Phase 3: the ladder runs at FIXED weights. No control loop.** | OLLA is closed-loop and its error signal (`cameraPxPerModule`) is a **receiver-side** metric, but only the sender can change rungs and D16 says no negotiation in v1. A controller with no observable cannot run. The research places fixed-weight ladders at T2/Phase 3 and weight adaptation at T4/Phase 5; an earlier revision collapsed the two. **Fixed weights (frame-area fractions): R1 (conservative v10-L) = 15%, R2 (nominal v15-L) = 60%, R3 (aggressive v20-L) = 25%. Never drop any rung below 10% in steady state.** | `link-adaptation` §10.2 |\n277\t| D18b | **Phase 5: adapt ladder weights from LOCAL metrics only — OLLA structure, 1:9 up/down asymmetry, ~1 s window, 2 s dwell, immediate hard step-down** | Closed-loop density control oscillates; profile selection stays a **stateless lookup** so there is no state machine to get stuck in. \"Local\" means the sender's own signals (frame timing, accelerometer à la COBRA), never receiver feedback. | `link-adaptation` §10.3 |\n278\t| D18c | **Assume 20–30% residual erasure. This is an ASSUMPTION about the channel, not a controlled target.** | Nothing in v1 observes erasure (D18a), so calling it a \"target\" was wrong. 20–30% is the evidence base's figure; driving it lower would mean the ladder is too conservative and throughput is being left unused. Dwell is sized to survive the **top** of the band (§8.1), and the repair code (§8.2) covers the tail beyond it. | `link-adaptation` §9.3 |\n279\t\n280\t---\n281\t\n282\t## 5. Invariants\n283\t\n284\tViolating one of these is a correctness bug, not a tuning choice. Each has an\n285\tenforcement mechanism, because an invariant nothing checks is a comment.\n286\t\n287\t| # | Invariant | Enforced by |\n288\t|---|---|---|\n289\t| **I1** | Fragment length **L** MUST NOT change within a session (D15) | Session type makes `L` `readonly`; property test asserts a mid-session change throws |\n290\t| **I2** | The degree distribution and the decoder MUST change together (D6); any distribution change MUST be simulated before merge | `sim/` assertions ported into the test suite; CI gate G4 |\n291\t| **I3** | Fountain indices MUST be derived from `(streamId, blockIndex, seq)`, never transmitted (D7) | Golden test vector `(streamId, blockIndex, seq) → index set`, bit-exact across implementations |\n292\t| **I4** | The file MUST NOT be fully materialised in memory on either side (D20) | Phase 1 flat-memory test over a synthetic 4 GB stream |\n293\t| **I5** | **Exactly one payload block is GE-active at a time; the manifest stream has its own separate GE context** (bf-28b) | Session type permits two concurrent GE contexts: `active` for payload blocks and `manifestActive` for manifest blocks. Payload block-switch policy (`bf-2t1k`) governs when to switch: hold until rank K or N consecutive higher-index packets (default N=32). The manifest uses reserved `blockIndex = 0xFFFFFF` and `PacketFlags.Manifest`, providing clean separation from payload blocks. This is necessary because manifest blocks are interleaved with payload blocks (§7.3), and both require fountain decoding. |\n294\t| **I6a** | **Block-layer** working set MUST stay ≤ 1 MB regardless of file size (528 KB at the adopted design: 264 KB payload GE context + 264 KB manifest GE context) | A5 headless block-layer memory assertion |\n295\t| **I6b** | **Whole-receiver** peak MUST stay ≤ 64 MB, and the decode pool MUST hold ≤ 4 in-flight `VideoFrame`s | Phase 3 instrumented run. A single 1080p RGBA frame is **7.9 MiB**, so this budget is dominated by the camera path, not the codec — which is why I6 had to be split |\n296\t| **I7** | Frames MUST be generated on demand, never pre-rendered (D24) | Ring buffer is bounded at 3; assertion on buffer depth |\n297\t| **I8** | A packet failing `fcrc` or `streamId` MUST be discarded, never applied | Unit test with corrupted and foreign packets |\n298\t| **I9** | A block MAY be written to OPFS before its hash arrives, but MUST NOT be surfaced to the user until verified | Test: blocks written before manifest arrives are not exported; verification failure prevents completion and triggers E-BLOCK-HASH |\n299\t| **I10** | Decoded output MUST be byte-identical to input | End-to-end property test, every phase |\n300\t\n301\t---\n302\t\n303\t## 6. Architecture\n304\t\n305\t### 6.1 Layering\n306\t\n307\t**Modulation is swappable**, and **the block layer bounds everything below it**.\n308\t\n309\t```\n310\t┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n311\t│ UI          role select · progress · file in/out · coach │\n312\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n313\t│ Session     metadata · compression · resume · verify     │\n314\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n315\t│ Block       file ⇄ 192 KB blocks · scheduling · bitmap   │\n316\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n317\t│ Fountain    LT encode (endless) / GF(2) GE decode        │\n318\t│             K = 768 · matrix 72.0 KB · CONSTANT          │\n319\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n320\t│ Framing     13-byte header + payload → packet bytes      │\n321\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n322\t│ Modulation  ◄──────────────────────── SWAPPABLE ────────►│\n323\t│   Stage 1   tiled monochrome QR                          │\n324\t│   Stage 2   + RGB channel tripling                       │\n325\t│   Stage 3   libcimbar-derived grid codec                 │\n326\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n327\t│ Transport   canvas render loop  /  camera capture loop   │\n328\t└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n329\t```\n330\t\n331\t```ts\n332\tinterface Modulation {\n333\t  readonly packetsPerFrame: number;     // 1 plain, ~15 tiled, ~45 tripled\n334\t  readonly bytesPerPacket: number;      // = 13 + L\n335\t  encodeFrame(packets: Uint8Array[]): ImageData;\n336\t  decodeFrame(frame: VideoFrame): Uint8Array[];   // 0..n — never throws\n337\t}\n338\t```\n339\t\n340\t`decodeFrame` returning fewer packets than `packetsPerFrame` is the **normal case**.\n341\tNothing above this layer may care.\n342\t\n343\t### 6.2 Threads and ownership\n344\t\n345\tLayer boundaries and thread boundaries are **not** the same, which is worth stating\n346\texplicitly because it is a common source of bugs:\n347\t\n348\t| Component | Thread | Owns |\n349\t|---|---|---|\n350\t| UI, canvas paint | main | display |\n351\t| Frame encoder | worker | ring buffer (depth 3, I7) |\n352\t| QR decode pool | N workers | `VideoFrame` — MUST `close()` each or the pipeline stalls |\n353\t| GE decoder | 1 worker | the 72 KB matrix; single-owner, no sharing |\n354\t| OPFS writer | worker | `createSyncAccessHandle` is worker-only |\n355\t\n356\t**Backpressure policy:** if decode falls behind capture, camera frames are **dropped, not\n357\tqueued**. A queued frame is stale by the time it decodes, and queuing turns a throughput\n358\tproblem into a memory problem. Dropped frames are erasures, which the fountain code\n359\talready absorbs.\n360\t\n361\t### 6.3 Sender pipeline\n362\t\n363\t```\n364\tFile ──► [sample: compressible?] ──► CompressionStream ──► OPFS staging\n365\t  │            (D8, skip if not)                              │\n366\t  └──────────────── or straight through ─────────────────────┘\n367\t                                                              │\n368\t                                   cut into 192 KB blocks (D19)\n369\t                                                              │\n370\t                 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n371\t                 ▼                                            ▼\n372\t        beacon (D17/D21) every ~2 s          per block: slice → K=768 fragments\n373\t        filename · size · blockCount           → LT encode (d ≤ 64, D25)\n374\t        blockSize · L · K · hash · flags       → header → tile\n375\t                 │                                            │\n376\t                 └──────────────► frame mixer ◄───────────────┘\n377\t                                       │\n378\t                          ladder of 2–4 profiles (D16)\n379\t                                       │\n380\t                              DC-balance (D10) ──► canvas\n381\t                                       │\n382\t                     display at ≤ ½ measured camera fps (D9/D14)\n383\t```\n384\t\n385\tThe sender **dwells** on each block (§8.1), then advances, looping the file\n386\tcontinuously. It never terminates on its own — it cannot know when the receiver is done.\n387\t\n388\t> **Beacon clarification:** The beacon is a **packet** (distinguished by `PacketFlags.Beacon` in its header), not a separate frame. The \"frame mixer\" shown above combines beacon tiles (QR-encoded beacon packets) with payload tiles into the same displayed frames. This ensures minimal overhead: the sender emits beacon packets every ~2 seconds by replacing a few payload tiles in regular frames, rather than interrupting transmission with dedicated beacon frames.\n389\t\n390\t#### 6.3.1 Frames are generated on demand (D24)\n391\t\n392\tEvery arrow above is a **generator**, not an array.\n393\t\n394\t- **No finite frame set exists.** The LT encoder is rateless; how many frames a transfer\n395\t  needs depends on channel loss and is unknowable in advance.\n396\t- **One pass would not fit.** 4 GB ≈ 550,000 frames; as 1080p `ImageData` that is\n397\t  **4.2 TB**, ~55 GB even as PNGs.\n398\t- **On-demand is cheap.** ~0.29 ms per v15 tile (from 1.53 ms at v40, mask pinned) ×\n399\t  15 tiles × 15 fps ≈ **65 ms/sec, ~7% of one core**, plus ~2.3 ms/sec to render, plus\n400\t  **fountain XOR: 3.4 KB/packet at d ≤ 64 (D25) = 0.8 MB/s** at this geometry's\n401\t  **450 packets/s** (15 tiles × 2 packets/tile × 15 fps, using the R2 nominal rung) —\n402\t  negligible, but only because of the cap. Uncapped it is 6.1 MB/s\n403\t  at K = 768, and was 91.8 MB/s at the old K = 16,384.\n404\t\n405\tBecause indices derive from a PRNG (D7), the sender is **stateless**: frame *N* generates\n406\tdirectly without replaying 1…*N*−1. That is what makes resume and repair nearly free.\n407\t\n408\t**Implementation:** worker generator → ring buffer (depth 3) → main thread paints via\n409\t`rAF`. Deeper buffering is wasted memory (I7).\n410\t\n411\t#### 6.3.2 Shape the code region to the CAMERA, not the screen\n412\t\n413\tThe receiver's camera has a fixed aspect and a fixed pixel count; the sender's screen has a different one. What matters is **camera px per module** (§2), and that is set by how much of the capture the code region fills. The 4 px/module decode cliff is measured: spike S3 showed 100% erasure at 1.5 camera px/module (0.0 KB/s), dropping to 78% at 2.25 camera px/module (4.0 KB/s). Properly shaping the code region clears the cliff and is the single biggest lever.\n414\t\n415\tA 1920×1080 landscape code region imaged by a portrait 1080×1920 capture yields **M = 0.5625** —\n416\tso 4 screen px/module is only 2.25 camera px/module, below the cliff. Rendering the *same*\n417\tpayload into a **portrait-shaped region** inverts this:\n418\t\n419\t| Code region on screen | M | To achieve 4 camera px/module | Tiles that fit | Payload/frame |\n420\t|---|---|---|---|---|\n421\t| 1920×1080 landscape | 0.56 | 7.1 screen px/module | 8 | 4.0 KB |\n422\t| 1080×1080 square | 1.00 | 4.0 screen px/module | 8 | 4.0 KB |\n423\t| **540×960 portrait** | **2.00** | **2.0 screen px/module** | **8** | **4.0 KB** |\n424\t\n425\t**How to read this table:** Each row shows a different code region shape. The \"To achieve 4 camera px/module\" column shows the screen px/module required to reach the cliff threshold given that region's magnification M. The \"Tiles that fit\" column shows how many tiles fit at that screen px/module. All rows are evaluated at the same camera px/module (4.0), so they can be compared directly.\n426\t\n427\t**What the table shows:** To clear the 4 camera px/module cliff, a portrait code region (M=2.0) needs only 2.0 screen px/module, while a naive landscape region (M=0.56) would need 7.1 screen px/module. At those respective screen px/module values, each region fits about 8 tiles and delivers ~4.0 KB/frame. The portrait region achieves the same camera px/module with fewer screen pixels per module, leaving more room for tiles — but all three geometries are equivalent when tuned for the same camera px/module target.\n428\t\n429\t**The sender MUST use the portrait-region layout by default.** The 540×960 portrait region is the primary code region, and **Phase 3's ≥ 20 KB/s gate MUST pass with this region and the receiver held portrait, unaided** — that is the default, unassisted case, not a stretch goal.\n430\t\n431\t**Packets-per-tile basis and the actual design.** The R2 nominal rung (v16-L, 60% of tiles in steady state per D18a) carries **2 packets per tile**. Each packet is 269 B (13-byte header + 256 B payload), so 2 packets = 538 B per tile, which fits within v16-L's 586 B capacity. The **user-visible payload** is 15 tiles × 2 packets/tile × 256 B = **7,680 B/frame ≈ 7.5 KB/frame**. The **8.6 KB/frame QR capacity** is 15 tiles × 586 B (v16-L capacity) = 8,790 B. At 15 fps, this geometry delivers **7.5 KB × 15 fps = 112.5 KB/s payload rate** (or ~113 KB/s) before fountain overhead and erasure loss.\n432\t\n433\t> **G7 gate target:** At the adopted design (15 tiles, 2 packets/tile, 15 fps), **7.5 KB user payload per frame** and **8.6 KB QR frame capacity** deliver **112.5 KB/s payload rate**.\n434\t\n435\t**Why 15 tiles when the table shows 8?** The table above shows the tile count that fits when targeting exactly 4 camera px/module. The actual design uses 15 tiles at ~1-2 screen px/module, which achieves ~2-2.5 camera px/module (below the 4.0 cliff threshold but still functional based on S3 measurements showing 78% erasure at 2.25 camera px/module delivering 4.0 KB/s). The design trades some pixel safety for higher tile count and throughput; the table illustrates the *relationship* between M, screen px/module, and camera px/module, not the exact design parameters.\n436\t\n437\t**Two independent approaches; do not compose them.** There are two ways to increase M:\n438\t\n439\t1. **Sender-side:** Shape the code region to match the receiver's orientation (540×960 portrait region for portrait receiver). This is the **primary, always-on path** — the sender uses this region by default.\n440\t2. **Receiver-side:** Physically rotate the receiver device (landscape orientation for landscape receiver). This gives M = 2.78 × sender's M.\n441\t\n442\t**Do not combine these approaches.** A sender-side portrait region (M=2.0) combined with a receiver-side landscape orientation would give M ≈ 5.6, achieving ~11 camera px/module at 2 screen px/module — 3× more than needed, and at half the tiles that geometry could carry. Use exactly one approach: either the sender-side portrait region (default) OR the receiver-side landscape rotation (optional), not both.\n443\t\n444\t**Receiver-side landscape is a free bonus, not a requirement.** Physically holding the receiver in landscape puts the screen's long axis on the camera's long axis — 1.78× more magnification for free. It is worth *offering* to a user willing to turn the phone. But the app MUST NOT depend on the user doing so: the sender-side portrait region (above) is the primary, always-on path, and landscape is strictly an optional upgrade for extra margin on top of it.\n445\t\n446\t**Orientation handling.** The sender does not configure the receiver's OS orientation — that is impossible without a back-channel. Instead, the sender shapes its code region for the expected receiver orientation (portrait by default), and the receiver's UI coaches the user to match that orientation (§11, `E-ORIENTATION`). For the optional landscape bonus, the receiver's surface coaches the user to turn the device sideways; a physical turn is required because sensor mapping follows the device body, not the UI.\n447\t\n448\t### 6.4 Receiver pipeline\n449\t\n450\t```\n451\tgetUserMedia ──► exposureCompensation:min (D14) ──► measure real fps (rVFC, ~1 s)\n452\t      │\n453\t      └──► requestVideoFrameCallback ──► MediaStreamTrackProcessor*\n454\t                                                │\n455\t                              ROI crop (conditional — see §6.4)\n456\t                                                │\n457\t                              ┌─────────────────┴──── Worker pool ────┐\n458\t                              ▼                                       ▼\n459\t                      zxing readBarcodes                     [Stage 2: split\n460\t                      (all symbols, .bytes)                   R/G/B, stretch, ×3]\n461\t                              │\n462\t                    header parse ──► fcrc ──► streamId lock ──► route by blockIndex\n463\t                              │                                        │\n464\t                     beacon? ──┴──► learn size/blocks/K/hash    payload ──► GE decoder\n465\t                                    (gates everything)\n466\t                                                        rank == K ──► write to OPFS\n467\t                                                                  ──► mark decode bitmap\n468\t                                                                  ──► verify hash (if manifest present)\n469\t                                                                  ──► mark verified bitmap\n470\t                                                                              │\n471\t                                            all blocks present & manifest decoded ──► verify all blocks\n472\t                                                                  ──► [decompress] ──► compute whole-file hash ──► compare with beacon ──► save (or E-FILE-HASH if mismatch)\n473\t```\n474\t\n475\t\\* `MediaStreamTrackProcessor` is **Chromium-only**; `requestVideoFrameCallback` +\n476\t`drawImage` is the universal fallback and MUST be implemented (§6.5).\n477\t\n478\t**Block-layer working set: 264.0 KB** — 72.0 KB matrix + 192.0 KB block — flat regardless\n479\tof file size. This is *not* the whole-receiver figure; see I6a/I6b in §5. The **total peak\n480\tworking set is 528.0 KB** when including the manifest GE context (72.0 KB matrix + 192.0 KB block)\n481\tand recover()'s second K*L array, still well under I6a's 1 MB limit (0.52×).\n482\t\n483\t> **G7 gate targets:** At the adopted design, **264.0 KB block-layer working set** (matrix + block) and **528.0 KB total peak working set** (payload + manifest GE contexts).\n484\t\n485\tThree rules that are cheap to implement and expensive to omit:\n486\t\n487\t- **Measure fps, never trust it.** `getSettings()` reports 30/60 while the camera\n488\t  delivers 15.\n489\t- **Crop to ROI before decoding — but the 9× is conditional.** Measured 8.6× (56.9 → 6.6 ms)\n490\t  *when the code occupies part of the frame*. Once the grid fills the frame — which is what\n491\t  you want for camera px/module — **the ROI is the frame and the win evaporates** (69 ms).\n492\t  ROI is a recovery mechanism for being too far away, not a throughput optimisation at the\n493\t  right distance. **Except at high capture resolution**, where a tight quad-crop is what keeps\n494\t  camera px/module high *and* pixel count bounded at once — there it is load-bearing, and must\n495\t  be far tighter than the spike's 35%-margin version.\n496\t- **Select capture resolution deliberately — it is a first-class tunable.** Measured knee:\n497\t  720p → 100% erasure (1.5 camera px/module, nothing decodes); 1080p → best goodput; 4K →\n498\t  zero empty frames but 194 ms decode and 1.1 fps, net *worse*. Decode is O(pixels), so more\n499\t  resolution is not free. `getUserMedia` defaults are **not** adequate: a Pixel 6 defaults to\n500\t  1080 on the *short* edge.\n501\t- **Shape the code region to the camera, not the screen (sender-side, §6.3.2).**\n502\t- **Never offer a torch button.** It measured a 3.6× fps gain, which makes it tempting,\n503\t  but an LED on a glossy screen creates a specular hotspot that destroys a region of the\n504\t  frame. `exposureCompensation` gets the same mechanism without glare.\n505\t\n506\t### 6.5 Module layout and dependency pins\n507\t\n508\tCommitted in Phase 0 so \"where does this go?\" is not re-litigated eight phases running.\n509\tNote the layer boundaries of §6.1 and the thread boundaries of §6.2 are **not** the same,\n510\tso the tree separates them explicitly.\n511\t\n512\t```\n513\tsrc/\n514\t  core/                 # pure, no DOM, no workers — the testable heart\n515\t    params.ts           # ⚠️ CRITICAL: rung table, validation guards, G7 diff targets\n516\t    session/            #   types.ts (SendSession, RecvSession from §7.4)\n517\t    fountain/           #   encoder.ts (was lt-encode.ts)  decoder.ts (was ge-decode.ts)  prng.ts\n518\t    block/              #   partition.ts\n519\t    frame/              #   header.ts  beacon.ts  crc.ts\n520\t    hash/               #   block-hash.ts  whole-file-hash.ts\n521\t    errors/             #   error-codes.ts (§11 error taxonomy)\n522\t    io/                 #   positional-write.ts (OPFS positional write for D20)\n523\t  modulation/           # the swappable layer (§6.1)\n524\t    types.ts            #   the Modulation interface — the ONLY contract above\n525\t    qr-tiled/           #   stage 1: qr-encoder.ts  zxing-config.ts\n526\t    qr-tiled/           #   qr-encoder-worker.ts  (encode worker)\n527\t    qr-colour/          #   stage 2 (not yet implemented)\n528\t    grid/               #   stage 3 (not yet implemented)\n529\t  workers/              # worker implementations for thread roles (§6.2)\n530\t    qr-encode.worker.ts  qr-decode-pool.ts  qr-decode.worker.ts  ge-benchmark.worker.ts\n531\t  platform/             # every capability probe and fallback lives here\n532\t    camera-pipeline.ts  storage.ts  export.ts  ge-benchmark.ts  health-check.ts\n533\t    init.ts  orientation.ts  capture-resolution.ts  simple-ge-runner.ts  version.ts\n534\t  ui/                   # role select, progress, coaching, pre-flight (not yet implemented)\n535\t  app.ts\n536\ttest/\n537\t  fixtures/             # conformance vectors (§14.3)\n538\t  degradation/          # synthetic blur/glare/tear generators\n539\tdocs/                   # plan, notes, research, sim\n540\t```\n541\t\n542\t**Missing from implementation (from original plan):**\n543\t- `core/fountain/degree.ts` — degree distribution logic (D6, D25)\n544\t- `core/block/bitmap.ts` — block bitmap for D22 resume\n545\t- `core/block/schedule.ts` — dwell scheduling (§8.1) and repair code (§8.2)\n546\t- `core/frame/repair-code.ts` — repair code format (§7.6, §8.2)\n547\t- `core/hash/stream-id.ts` — streamId derivation (§7.5)\n548\t- `modulation/qr-tiled/layout.ts` — tile layout logic\n549\t- `modulation/qr-tiled/ladder.ts` — D16 ladder rung logic\n550\t- `workers/opfs.worker.ts` — OPFS worker (may be inline elsewhere)\n551\t\n552\t**Module-to-phase map.** Each unwritten core module is assigned to a specific phase based on when its functionality is first required by exit criteria or invariants. This map prevents \"module exists but has no owner\" gaps.\n553\t\n554\t| Module | Phase | Rationale |\n555\t|---|---|---|\n556\t| `core/frame/beacon.ts` | **1** | Beacon packet encoding/decoding (§7.2, D17/D21) is framing — Phase 1's \"framing\" deliverable. Required for the receiver to learn file metadata (`streamId`, `blockCount`, `K`, etc.) before it can interpret any payload packet. |\n557\t| `core/hash/stream-id.ts` | **1** | `streamId` derivation (§7.4, D7) is required by the fountain encoder's PRNG seeding. Phase 1's \"LT encode\" and \"GE decode\" cannot work without `streamId`, and I3's conformance vector depends on it. |\n558\t| `core/hash/block-hash.ts` | **1** | Per-block hashes (§7.3) are the only application-layer integrity check on payload bytes (§7.1). Phase 1's \"byte-exact\" requirement (property tests) and I9's verification invariant cannot be enforced without them. |\n559\t| `core/block/schedule.ts` | **4** | Dwell scheduling (§8.1) and repair code targeting (§8.2) are large-file machinery. Phase 4's A5 (synthetic 4 GB), A6 (resume), and A7 (repair) exit criteria require block scheduling. |\n560\t| `core/frame/repair-code.ts` | **4** | Repair code format (§7.6, §8.2) is the human-mediated recovery path. Phase 4's A7 exit criterion (\"Only the missing blocks retransmit\") requires encoding/decoding repair codes. |\n561\t\n562\t**Rules.** `core/` MUST NOT import from `modulation/`, `workers/`, `platform/` or `ui/` —\n563\tit is the layer the property tests own. Nothing outside `modulation/` may reference QR\n564\t(§6.1 modulation is swappable). Every browser capability check lives in\n565\t`platform/capabilities.ts`, never inline at a call site, so §16.1's platform matrix has\n566\texactly one implementation.\n567\t\n568\t**Dependency contract.** Exact-pinned, no ranges, no post-install scripts (gate G3).\n569\t\n570\t| Dependency | Pin | If unavailable |\n571\t|---|---|---|\n572\t| `zxing-wasm` | exact version + SRI on the `.wasm`. **MUST call `setZXingModuleOverrides({ locateFile })` pointing at a bundle-local, service-worker-precached `.wasm`.** See the general WASM rule below | Fatal on the receiver — surface `E-WASM-LOAD`; the sender still works |\n573\t| `incremental-wasm-hash` | exact version + SRI on the `.wasm`. **MUST be bundle-local, service-worker-precached, and loaded via bundle-local overrides (not default CDN paths).** See the general WASM rule below | Fatal on the receiver — surface `E-WASM-LOAD`; per-block hashes alone are insufficient for byte-exact reconstruction per concept.md constraint 4 |\n574\t| `node-qrcode` | exact version | Fatal on the sender; the receiver still works |\n575\t| `CompressionStream` | platform | Skip compression (D8 is already conditional) |\n576\t| `MediaStreamTrackProcessor` | platform | Fall back to `requestVideoFrameCallback` + `drawImage` — MUST be implemented, it is not Chromium-only |\n577\t| OPFS | platform | Refuse large files; cap at in-memory size and say so |\n578\t| Wake Lock | platform | Warn before a long transfer (`E-WAKELOCK-LOST`) |\n579\t\n580\t> ### ⚠️ EVERY WASM dependency MUST be bundle-local and SRI-pinned\n581\t>\n582\t> **This is a general rule, not specific to zxing.** Any package that loads WASM from a\n583\t> CDN by default voids the entire premise. The receiver:\n584\t>\n585\t> 1. makes a **third-party network request mid-session** — voiding T7, concept.md\n586\t>    constraint 1, and the README's \"provably no exfiltration\";\n587\t> 2. **fails completely in airplane mode** — i.e. in the flagship air-gapped use case (A8);\n588\t> 3. **executes remotely-fetched WASM** — precisely the supply-chain surface T5 exists for.\n589\t>\n590\t> **Every WASM dependency MUST:**\n591\t>\n592\t> - Be bundled with the application (not fetched from a CDN)\n593\t> - Have its `.wasm` file SRI-pinned in the lockfile (integrity hash)\n594\t> - Be precached by the service worker for offline operation\n595\t> - Be loaded via bundle-local overrides, not default CDN paths\n596\t>\n597\t> **Current WASM dependencies covered by this rule:**\n598\t>\n599\t> - `zxing-wasm`: MUST call `setZXingModuleOverrides({ locateFile })` pointing at a\n600\t>   bundle-local, service-worker-precached `.wasm`\n601\t> - `incremental-wasm-hash` (the whole-file hasher): MUST be bundle-local and\n602\t>   service-worker-precached; used for the mandatory whole-file hash (§7.2)\n603\t>\n604\t> §14.4's no-network assertion covers this — it MUST exercise every WASM code path to\n605\t> detect CDN fetches. For zxing, this means the assertion must perform a decode; for the\n606\t> hasher, it must hash a non-empty stream.\n607\t\n608\t**Cross-origin isolation.** The pipeline uses transferable `VideoFrame`s and\n609\t`ArrayBuffer`s, **not** `SharedArrayBuffer` — so COOP/COEP headers are **not** required.\n610\tThis is deliberate: requiring them would constrain static hosting for no gain. Any future\n611\tuse of `SharedArrayBuffer` is a hosting decision, not just a code change.\n612\t\n613\t### 6.6 The luma-vs-colour disagreement, and how it is resolved\n614\t\n615\t| | `custom-codec-engineering.md` §7.2 | `beyond-qr-optical-channels.md` §6.6 |\n616\t|---|---|---|\n617\t| Colour cell penalty under 4:2:0 | 2× linear (4× area) — **derived** | 1.25× linear (1.56× area) — **measured** |\n618\t| Verdict | luma-only wins ~1.95× | RGB-tripling wins **1.98×** |\n619\t\n620\tThe measured result is better founded and the mechanism convincing: **chroma decimation\n621\tis a low-pass filter, not a deletion.** A binary chroma pattern at 5 px/module presents\n622\t2.5 chroma samples per module — above Nyquist; at 4 px/module exactly 2.0, right at\n623\tNyquist, which is where the measurement breaks. The \"2× per axis\" rule over-corrects by\n624\trestoring the *original* sampling density rather than staying above Nyquist in the\n625\tdecimated grid.\n626\t\n627\tAlso weighing against luma-only: 8-level luma measured **unusable** under handheld blur\n628\t(21.2% symbol error at 5 px/cell) vs **0.00%** for saturated 8-colour at 4 px/cell; and\n629\t**libcimbar spends 2 of its 6 bits per cell on colour**, with its deprecated 8-colour\n630\tmode benchmarking *faster*.\n631\t\n632\t**Resolution (D11): neither document decides.** A calibration probe measures the device\n633\tat session start. Where the luma-side note is unambiguously right: **AWB warps colour in\n634\tthree non-monotonic dimensions** and cannot be locked on iOS, so a per-frame in-band\n635\tcolour reference is **not optional** for Stage 2.\n636\t\n637\t---\n638\t\n639\t## 7. Data model\n640\t\n641\t### 7.1 Payload packet header — 13 bytes\n642\t\n643\t| Offset | Size | Field | Notes |\n644\t|---|---|---|---|\n645\t| 0 | 1 | `magic_ver` | 4-bit magic + 4-bit wire version. Rejects foreign QR instantly. See §16.3 for version skew. |\n646\t| 1 | 1 | `flags` | packet type (payload/beacon), reserved |\n647\t| 2 | 4 | `streamId` | Identifies the **file**. Seeds the PRNG; receiver locks it on first sight. Derivation: §7.5 |\n648\t| 6 | 3 | `blockIndex` | 16.7 M blocks × 192 KB = **3.0 TB** addressable — beyond any practical transfer (1 TB is 117 days) |\n649\t| 9 | 3 | `seq` | Sequence **within the block**; with `streamId`+`blockIndex` derives the index set |\n650\t| 12 | 1 | `fcrc` | CRC-8 — rejects a mis-decode before it poisons the matrix |\n651\t\n652\t`K`, `L` and the index set remain **derived, never transmitted** (I3).\n653\t\n654\t**`fcrc` covers bytes 0–11 only — the header, NOT the payload.** This is deliberate: CRC-8\n655\tover 269 bytes would be weak anyway, and the header is what must be trusted before a packet\n656\tis routed to a block. But the consequence must be stated plainly:\n657\t\n658\t> **A packet whose header is intact and whose 256-byte payload is corrupted passes `fcrc`\n659\t> unconditionally and poisons the GE matrix.** `fcrc` is a routing guard, not an integrity\n660\t> check.\n661\t\n662\tPayload integrity therefore rests on exactly two things: QR's own Reed–Solomon (which makes\n663\tan undetected symbol error rare, but not impossible) and **the per-block hash (§7.3), which\n664\tis the sole application-layer check on payload bytes.** The manifest-based hash verification\n665\tensures corrupted blocks are detected before completion: a block that reaches rank K but fails\n666\tits hash is never surfaced to the user and triggers re-collection (`E-BLOCK-HASH`, §11, E12).\n667\tI9 enforces that unverified blocks written to OPFS are never exported or made visible to\n668\tthe user until the manifest arrives and verification succeeds. A test MUST corrupt a payload\n669\tbyte and assert the block hash catches it — corrupting only header bytes, as the current\n670\tsuite does, cannot detect this class at all.\n671\t\n672\t### 7.2 Beacon packet (D17/D21)\n673\t\n674\tEmitted every ~2 s at the most conservative profile. Everything the receiver needs before\n675\tit can interpret any payload packet:\n676\t\n677\t| Field | Size | Notes |\n678\t|---|---|---|\n679\t| `streamId` | 4 | Must match payload packets |\n680\t| `wireVersion` | 1 | Full version, not the 4-bit nibble |\n681\t| `originalSize` | 6 | Original uncompressed file size — 281 TB addressable, **MUST be bounds-checked** (§12, T1) |\n682\t| `payloadLen` | 6 | Actual payload length after compression (if enabled); required to compute the last block's short length — `blockCount * blockSize` is an upper bound only |\n683\t| `blockSize`, `blockCount` | 3 + 3 | Yields K (blockSize / L). Last block short length is derived from `payloadLen`, not from blockSize alone. |\n684\t| `fragmentLen` (L) | 2 | Fixed for the session (I1) |\n685\t| `degreeCap` | 1 | D25; receiver MUST use the same cap |\n686\t| `flags` | 1 | compressed / hash alg / colour profile |\n687\t| `blockHashLen` | 1 | Per-block hash truncation length |\n688\t| `wholeFileHash` | 32 | **Mandatory.** concept.md constraint 4 makes byte-exact reconstruction non-negotiable and names this as the verification. An earlier revision made it optional \"on very large files\" — i.e. dropped the guarantee exactly where E5 (source mutated during a 10-hour read) is most likely and the stakes are highest. Computed on the **decompressed reassembly** (after decompression, if compression is enabled; otherwise on the received blocks directly). The sender hashes the original file by streaming it through an incremental WASM hasher; the receiver hashes its decompressed output and compares. The hash covers the final user-visible output, not intermediate compressed data. If decompression fails (E15), the hash cannot be evaluated and the compressed artefact is kept unverified. |\n689\t| `manifestHash` | 4 | **Mandatory.** CRC-32 of the manifest data (§7.3). Roots the cryptographic chain: **beacon → manifest → blocks → whole file**. Without this, a corrupted manifest packet would cause wrong block hashes, leading to infinite E12 failures with no error code or termination. The beacon already carries 32 bytes; adding 4 more is negligible. |\n690\t| `filenameLen` | 1 | Length prefix for filename field |\n691\t| `filename` | var | UTF-8 filename, **sanitised** (§12, T2). Capped at 128 bytes / 32 codepoints. See truncation rules below. |\n692\t| `mimeTypeLen` | 1 | Length prefix for MIME type field |\n693\t| `mimeType` | var | UTF-8 MIME type. Capped at 58 bytes / 14 codepoints. |\n694\t| `beaconCRC` | 4 | **Mandatory.** CRC-32 covering all beacon fields above. Validated before any beacon metadata is trusted. |\n695\t\n696\t**Beacon size bound calculation (R1's 256-byte payload):**\n697\t- Fixed fields: 64 bytes (streamId, wireVersion, originalSize, payloadLen, blockSize, blockCount, fragmentLen, degreeCap, flags, blockHashLen, wholeFileHash, manifestHash)\n698\t- CRC-32: 4 bytes (beacon integrity)\n699\t- Length prefixes: 2 bytes (filenameLen, mimeTypeLen)\n700\t- **Available for filename + mimeType: 256 − 64 − 4 − 2 = 186 bytes**\n701\t\n702\t**Allocation:**\n703\t- Filename: 128 bytes max, 32 UTF-8 codepoints max\n704\t- MIME type: 58 bytes max, 14 UTF-8 codepoints max\n705\t- Total: 186 bytes (exactly fits available space)\n706\t\n707\t**Filename truncation strategy (T2):**\n708\t1. **Strip path separators, control bytes, and leading dots** — prevents directory traversal and filesystem attacks\n709\t2. **Truncate to 32 UTF-8 codepoints max** — conservative bound ensuring we never exceed 128 bytes (worst case: 32 × 4 = 128)\n710\t3. **Preserve file extension when possible** — if truncating, keep \".ext\" suffix for usability\n711\t4. **Validate UTF-8 byte length** — ensure final encoded string fits in 128-byte beacon budget\n712\t5. **Fallback to \"received-file\"** — if filename is empty after sanitization\n713\t\n714\tThis strategy ensures the beacon never overflows R1's 256-byte payload while accommodating common filenames and MIME types. A 255-byte UTF-8 filename (legal on most filesystems) is safely truncated with no ambiguity.\n715\t\n716\tThe receiver shows \"acquiring…\" until its first beacon.\n717\t\n718\t### 7.3 The block-hash manifest — how per-block hashes reach the receiver\n719\t\n720\tI9, E12, §6.4, §8.3 and §7.4 all depend on per-block hashes, and §7.1 establishes they are\n721\tthe *only* application-layer check on payload bytes. Nothing in the wire format carried\n722\tthem: the 13-byte header has no room, and the beacon carries only `blockHashLen`.\n723\t\n724\t**A 4 GB file has 21,845 blocks. Even 4-byte hashes are 87 KB — far beyond a beacon.**\n725\t\n726\t**Resolution: hashes travel as a manifest, fountain-coded like any other block.**\n727\t\n728\t| Property | Value |\n729\t|---|---|\n730\t| Transport | A dedicated **manifest stream**, `blockIndex = 0xFFFFFF`, distinguished by `PacketFlags.Manifest` |\n731\t| Contents | `blockCount × blockHashLen` truncated hashes, in block order |\n732\t| Integrity | **Mandatory validation via beacon's `manifestHash` field (§7.2)**. The beacon carries a 4-byte CRC-32 of the manifest data. After decoding the manifest, the receiver MUST compute its CRC-32 and compare against the beacon's `manifestHash`. A mismatch indicates corruption and MUST cause the manifest to be discarded and re-decoded. This prevents infinite E12 failures from corrupted manifest data. |\n733\t| `blockHashLen` | **4 bytes.** Per-block false accept 2⁻³², ~5×10⁻⁶ across 21,845 blocks — comfortably below the whole-file hash's job |\n734\t| Coding | **Fixed K=768 multi-block stream** — `blockCount_manifest = ceil(blockCount × blockHashLen / BLOCK)`, same LT encoder, same GE decoder.
